name: Lofty Wood
reason: The source's mythical 'Jianmu' wood (a legendary divine tree) was renamed 'Lofty Wood' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A wood-type treasure said to rival any Divine Weapon, wielded by Janet as an extension of her own will; she can reshape it at will, weaving cages and other constructs from it. House Kincaid once tried and failed to draw it out of her. It is named as one of four legendary woods, alongside the Ray Wood of the east, the Sunrest Wood of the west, and the Aetherwood of the south, with the Lofty Wood hailing from the north.

name: Saint-Killing Spear
reason: The source weapon 'Holy Spear of Slaughter' (also rendered 'Holy Spear of Massacre'/'Sacred Spear of Slaughter'), Ming Dao's spear, was renamed 'Saint-Killing Spear' for a sharper Western fantasy register.
description: A legendary spear of the Demon Night wielded by Slade (source: Ming Dao) in the final arc. Far more than an ordinary treasure, it glows when its wielder unleashes his ultimate attacks and can swat volleys of arrows out of the air; Slade believes himself unbeatable with it in hand.

name: Elder Imogen
reason: The source elder's informal title-name 'Granny Yu' was localized to 'Elder Imogen', a dignified US-register name befitting a venerable female sect leader.
description: The leader of Cloud Hall, Tia's master and the sect's former head, and one of the strongest warriors in the Life-and-Death Realm. She eventually passes leadership of Cloud Hall to Tia, giving her free rein and promising to step in only in the direst emergencies; she also clearly sees Tia's feelings for Zane.

name: Preston
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Preston' conveys an arrogant young noble; the surname 'Sterling' ties him to House Sterling, matching the source's inner sect disciple surnamed Qiu.
description: An arrogant antagonist from House Sterling encountered during the Sky Forest/demon-hunting arc (Eps 110-130). A powerful 'creature of nature' (Xiantian-stage) senior disciple, he taunts and threatens Zane, but his confidence dissolves when he learns Zane has already slain a Demon Commander.

name: Prince
issues: Standalone 'Prince' is an extraction fragment: every sampled mention belongs to composite titles (Third Prince, Seventh Prince, Sixth Prince, Crown Prince), which are distinct characters of the imperial succession arc.
reason: Generic title fragment, not an entity in its own right; the individual princes should be tracked under their full titles or names (e.g. Connor, the Seventh Prince).

name: Apex of Sword Intent
reason: The source cultivation concept 'Perfect Sword Intent' (also rendered 'Perfect Sword Essence') was renamed 'Apex of Sword Intent' for a more dramatic Western fantasy register.
description: The highest comprehension of sword intent a swordsman can reach. Mastering it pulled Zane into the Sword Tempering Pool and transformed his swordsmanship into a devastating fusion of skill and cosmic energy; Finn later attains it as well, making Alistair's 'Accomplished Sword Intent' seem ordinary by comparison.

name: Blood Fiend Emperor
reason: The source epithet 'Blood Demon Emperor' was localized as 'Blood Fiend Emperor', softening 'Demon' to 'Fiend' to distinguish him from the show's demon races while keeping the menacing register.
description: A long-vanished ancient powerhouse whose legacy drives the ruins arc around Eps 378-607. He left behind a secret manuscript detailing a Tier Five Cultivation Method, part of his treasury hidden in the Sixth-Grade Sect ruins, and a colossal puppet built from modified Drake's teeth; before its collapse, his organization could have dominated several regions.

name: Phoebe
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xia Shuang' was fully localized to 'Phoebe', a soft feminine US-origin name fitting a young woman of the Demon Night.
description: A girl of the Demon Night clan who appears during the Sea God Continent arc (Eps 565-666), attending her clan's Queen and uneasy that the Queen travels with a human. She later reappears in the Cursed Land, helping Zane find a way out.

name: Orc
reason: The source's 'Beast Race' warriors were localized as 'Orcs', a familiar Western fantasy race label; the axe-wielding Beast Race War Reverend of the Sin Tower arc becomes the Orc opponents Zane faces.
description: A brutish warrior race encountered in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 569-637), known for massive axes, innate berserk abilities rooted in their beastly bloodline, and top-grade Mythic weaponry. Zane fights several of them in the ranked tower battles, including the berserk Orc War Lord.

name: Orc War Lord
reason: The source's axe-wielding 'Beast Race War Reverend' opponent was localized as the 'Orc War Lord', mapping the War Reverend rank to the Western 'War Lord'.
description: A berserk Orc champion Zane battles in the Tower of Sin trials (Eps 621-637), a twin-axe-wielding powerhouse of the Orc race's War Lord rank.

name: Callan
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Huo Chen' was fully localized to 'Callan', a US-origin name fitting a young royal; his sibling tie to Fiona mirrors Huo Chen and Huo Yuner in the source.
description: The Wind Crown Prince and Fiona's brother, overshadowed by his famous sister and barely acknowledged by the other crown princes. During the Feather Emperor's Secret Realm arc (Eps 840-910) he hauls around a giant, nearly indestructible lodestone (source: the Divine Magnetic Stone) from his storage ring, using it to block half a million poisoned arrows and earning the group's grudging respect.

name: Seymour
reason: The source cultivator's Daoist sobriquet 'Wuyue Sanren' (Wanderer Wuyue) was fully localized to 'Seymour', a distinguished-sounding US name; his Exquisite Jade Sword became the 'Emerald Sword'.
description: A ruthless master swordsman in the Immortal Mansion arc (Eps 152-156) who wields the Emerald Sword (source: Exquisite Jade Sword). After ambushing a rival master and standing alone as the victor, he turns his blade on Zane, declaring that only one of them can leave the desperate battle alive, and forces Zane onto the defensive with relentless speed and skill.

name: Frey
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhuge Feng' was fully localized to 'Frey', a short, proud-sounding US-origin name; his Family Zhuge 'Seven Mysterious' sword technique became the 'Sevenfold Blade'.
description: A Skyreach Sect disciple with a reputation for strength whose power had recently grown (Eps 169-176). Wielding the Sevenfold Blade, a seven-sword technique, he attacks Zane together with Vivian, but Zane's corrupted sword severs his connection to his blades one by one, sealing his defeat; the fallout of their clash leads into the sect trial arc.

name: Arcane Aurora
reason: The source training hazard 'Primary Magnetic Aurora' (magnetic auroras) was renamed 'Arcane Aurora' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: Relentless waves of pure energy, drawn from glacial heartstones and refined to extreme stability, used as a sword-training gauntlet (Eps 223-253). The blasts react only to sword intent, and withstanding them in quantity marks a warrior's training level; Zane and Zachary battle through wave after wave of them.

name: Jasper
issues: Split name reuse: 'Jasper' covers two different characters. In Eps ~236-285 'Master Jasper' is a Skyreach Sect elder observing the sword competition beside Sir Kenneth; in Eps 1063-1216 'Jasper Reed' is the top disciple of Cloudswallow Hall (source: Xue Muyang). The dossier merges both under one name; this row records Jasper Reed.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xue Muyang' was fully localized to 'Jasper Reed', a polished US-origin name fitting a celebrated top disciple.
description: Jasper Reed is the top warrior of Cloudswallow Hall, record-holder for a power output thirty-two times that of a standard Soul Realm warrior, easily ten times stronger than Gorman. When he passes through the Crimson Afterglow Ring it blazes with blinding light (Ep 1063), and he is counted among the elite talents, alongside Layla of The Mist Palace, who watch Zane's feats in disbelief.

name: Dragon's Keep
reason: The source location 'Dragon Castle' was renamed 'Dragon's Keep' to fit the Western medieval-fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A sprawling military complex housing thousands of barracks for the various squads, where Zane serves during the early squad arc (Eps 63-97). It is the site where the Diabolic Duo was killed, and squad discipline there is strict enough that desertion or murdered comrades would not be let slide.

name: Transcendent Divine Might
reason: The source term 'transcendent divine might' was carried over verbatim, as it already fit the adaptation's fantasy register.
description: The rarest class of technique in the setting, creatable only by a Supreme Lord. Mastering one is a lifetime achievement even for rulers; examples include the Star Plucking Technique practiced by Gideon and the Forceful Crystal Armor that Zane's father spent a lifetime mastering.

name: Nether God Shadow
reason: The source technique name 'Nether God Shadow' (also rendered 'Dark God Shadow') was retained verbatim, as it already suited the adaptation's register.
description: A technique of Zane's late-story arsenal (Eps 1060-1281) that releases ghostly figures from his blade, each a near-perfect copy of himself moving with his exact intent. He can field over a dozen at once, using them for coordinated strikes or to overwhelm opponents, though powerful enemies such as the Tiger-Taming Sentinels can shatter them outright.

name: Faith Energy
reason: The source term 'power of faith' (occasionally 'faith energy') was standardized as 'Faith Energy' for the adaptation.
description: A green energy offered up by believers through prayer, painstakingly collected by secret sects such as the Radiant Light Sect in Auspice City using specialized Divine Weapon containers (Eps 1124-1180). It is the only thing that allows the Ancestral Dragon to truly grow, and the dragon devours an entire hoard of it in one raid.

name: Wallace
reason: The source cultivator's title-name 'Heartless Monk' was fully localized to 'Wallace', a plain US-origin name, dropping the monk epithet to fit the Western setting.
description: A confident Soul Sea Realm warrior who leads an expedition to a hidden sect's ruins (Eps 772-808), having personally invited his old friend Master Abel (source: the Star-Sword Esteemed Cultivator) along for the ride. Sharp and decisive, he memorizes routes at a glance and presses forward without slowing.

name: Outer Disciple
reason: The source rank 'Outer Sect disciple' was streamlined to 'Outer Disciple' for the adaptation's sect hierarchy.
description: The entry-level rank of the Skyreach Sect, below Core Apprentice and the Varsity. Zane spends his early arcs (Eps 13-117) as an Outer Disciple, and feats like killing a Demonic Grunt or clearing a Razor swarm at that rank are considered extraordinary.

name: Varsity
reason: The source rank 'Inner Sect disciple' was localized as 'Varsity', borrowing US school-sports register (Varsity vs. pledge) for the sect's senior-disciple tier.
description: The senior disciple tier of the Skyreach Sect and rival sects such as Misty Peak (Eps 82-122). Varsity members operate in coordinated squads, hunt beasts for crystal cores, and outrank pledges; even they are barred from facing the greater demons of The Crucible alone.

name: Armory
issues: One label covers two distinct locations: the weapons facility of the early sect arc (Eps 104, 153, near the Alchemist's Laboratory) and the Armory inside the late-story keep, opened by the token of fire and tied to weaponsmithing skill (Eps 1173-1236). Possible merged entity.
reason: Generic weapons-hall locations in the source (e.g. halls of 'Profound Armaments') were localized under the single label 'Armory'.
description: A weapons repository name used in two eras of the show: an early huge hall of tactical-grade and higher weapons that Zane browses (Ep 104), and a sealed late-story Armory linked to the token of fire, which only a qualified weaponsmith is fit to control (Eps 1173-1197).

name: House Solomon
issues: Master-sheet notes drift between 'Helen's family' and 'Ingrid's extended circle', consistent with the known batch error where 'Helen' was mistakenly used for Ingrid (a separate, real Helen of House Solomon also exists).
reason: The source's 'Family Zhu', famous for its needle techniques, was localized as 'House Solomon', a Western noble-house name fitting the adaptation's Legacy House system.
description: A prestigious weaponsmithing noble house famous for its needle and concealed-weapon masters, mirroring the source Family Zhu's renowned needle techniques. It is Ingrid's house, and its Revelation Pins can spot a demon in an instant; its elders are influential enough that a marriage alliance could restore House Moon's fortunes, yet they refuse to restrict Ingrid's own choice.

name: Heaven
reason: Generic common noun/concept: the sampled mentions are exclamations ('Heaven has eyes'), the cosmic 'Heavens', and the 'Heaven' token of the Elysian Keep's eight-token set, not a single trackable entity.

name: Saint
issues: The label is also used in the master sheet for a 'Saint-level' talent rank (Eps 485+), distinct from the honorific usage in the trial arc; usage should be monitored for conflation.
reason: The source honorific 'Zhenren' (rendered 'Perfected'/'Reverend', e.g. Zhenren Tianqiong, Reverend Zi Qing) was localized as 'Saint', a Western honorific for the sect's most venerated masters.
description: An exalted title held by the most venerated masters of the sect world, such as Saint Viana and Saint Aldric, who preside over trials and command deference far above Acolytes (Eps 171-189). Zane's clash with the Saints over Elara's imprisonment in Infernal Peak drives the Mount Judgment arc; the master sheet also records a rare 'Saint-level' talent rank.

name: Nether Phantom
reason: The source creature 'Black Nightmare' (whose 'Black Nightmare Essences' Luo Zheng hoards) was renamed 'Nether Phantom' for a more evocative Western fantasy register.
description: Dark, tar-like creatures infesting confined worlds such as the Death Road (Eps 386-476), which hunt anything alive and are drawn by Vitality, draining and consuming their victims. They can be destroyed by heavenly thunder or absorbed by Corrupt Vitality, and leave behind raw essences so corrosive they would destroy the organs of anyone who swallowed one; Zane amasses hundreds of these essences.

name: Elite House
reason: The source institution 'Cloud Hall's Elite Hall' was localized as 'Elite House', aligning with the adaptation's House terminology.
description: The elite training division of Red Cloud Hall that Zane, Finn, and Patrick join (Eps 407-995), whose fresh disciples train in token-access rooms while finding their footing. Zane openly declares he will challenge everyone in it, making enemies of the entire Elite House, which prides itself on having no weaklings.
